working_set_correction.finding: Three of the four declared working-set globs match nothing on disk. `app/api/webhooks/music-institutional/**`, `app/api/webhooks/music-licensing/**` and `app/api/webhooks/music-rights-admin/**` do not exist. `find app/api/webhooks -type f` returns only music-marketplace/[partner], music-royalty-payouts, and supabase/notifications plus two test files. The three deferred partner ingress routes are mounted by their owning feature surface instead, and the record was written by hand before that was established.
working_set_correction.why_corrected: These are the only three routes the task title and AC-1 name: the advanced partner ingress routes that still carried an unsigned-bypass flag. They are integrations-owned, are named as the three siblings in the INTG-009 checkpoint, and are already classified in the integrations route inventory as integrations-owned. The task's intent is unambiguous, so the paths were corrected rather than the scope narrowed. No other `app/api/webhooks/**` route was touched.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Record the deferred disposition of the three advanced partner routes - unsigned flag, acknowledge-on-collision, unredacted payload - and confirm each is permanently 503 while advanced_music_webhooks is disabled.
evidence: __tests__/integrations/webhook-deferred-partner-certification.test.ts — 43 cases over the three routes, gate forced open with a test double.
`npm run agents:validate -- --strict` -> validated 18 agents, 216 tasks, 100 pending handoffs, 0 warnings, 0 errors.
Scoped `npx tsc -p <scoped tsconfig over the three routes and __tests__/integrations/**>` -> exit 0, 0 diagnostics.
acceptance_criteria.result: Reachable? No. Permanently 503, and each route is proven twice over.
reachability_proof: `isLaunchCapabilityAvailable` returns `false` for any `explicitlyApproved` value unless status is 'enabled' or 'pilot' (lib/config/launch-capabilities.ts:195-202). `advanced_music_webhooks` is `status: 'disabled', exposure: 'none'` (lines 56-60), and `isAuditFeatureApproved('advanced_webhooks')` delegates to it with the env approval as the second argument (lib/config/audit-feature-gates.ts:27-31). Therefore no value of FEATURE_AUDIT_ADVANCED_WEBHOOKS_APPROVED can open it. Asserted at runtime, not only by reading: the suite calls the real `isAuditFeatureApproved` with 'true', '1', 'on' and unset and gets false every time, and separately asserts `auditFeatureUnavailable` returns 503.

Each route consumes the gate as its first statement, before `request.text()`, before any env secret read, and before the service-role client is constructed, so a 503 cannot consume a body, touch a secret, or open a database session.

Second, independent barrier: none of the three receipt ledgers (music_institutional_partner_events, music_licensing_partner_events, music_rights_admin_partner_events) nor their outbox/invoice/agreement siblings exist in the active migration chain. `rg -l` over supabase/migrations returns zero files; the only definitions are in supabase/migration-archive/pre-reconciliation-local-only-2026-08-20/ with manifest status `local_only_unapplied`. Forcing the gate open without first applying the schema would 500 on the claim insert, not process a delivery.
acceptance_criteria.decision: FIX, not defer. Applied the INTG-009 pattern to all three routes rather than carrying the defect as debt.
acceptance_criteria.decision_reason: Three reasons. (1) It is the same defect class INTG-009 already fixed on the two enabled sibling routes, and the fix is mechanical reuse of code that already exists in this domain — `redactCredentialMaterial` and the `resolveClaim` shape. Divergence between four structurally identical partner routes is itself a defect. (2) The unsigned flag is one env var from a live unauthenticated-ingress bypass, which is exactly the latent launch defect AC-1 forbids leaving unowned; INTG-006 preserved it deliberately as fixture behaviour and INTG-009 then removed the marketplace twin, so the siblings were left inconsistent rather than intentionally deferred. (3) The change is provably inert: the routes are unconditionally 503, so no live behaviour can change and the fix carries zero launch risk. Deferring would have saved nothing and left a single-env-var bypass with no owner.

defects_found: SIGNATURE: `MUSIC_INSTITUTIONAL_WEBHOOK_ALLOW_UNSIGNED === 'true'` with no configured secret fell through to full processing, persisting the row with signature_verified: false and answering 200.

REPLAY: `if (isUniqueViolation(error)) return { idempotent: true }` answered a collision without reading processing_status/processed_at, so a delivery that claimed and then failed was acknowledged as done and its side effect (fund.nav.finalized outbox insert) was never applied.

COMPLETION: `.update(...).eq('id', stored.id)` was checked for `error` only, so a completion write landing on zero rows (deleted receipt, concurrently changed status) returned 200 and reported success.

REDACTION: the full provider payload was persisted verbatim in music_institutional_partner_events.raw_payload and in the music_institutional_outbox_events payload — a durable, service-role-readable copy of an unauthenticated boundary input.
per_route.fix: Unsigned flag removed; an unconfigured secret is unconditionally 503. Claim collision resolved by a `resolveClaim` helper that reads the completion marker first: processed acknowledges with zero side effects, a `failed` or a `received`-past-300s claim is atomically reclaimed and resumes, an unreadable marker or unresolvable collision is 500. Completion update now returns its row via `.select('id').maybeSingle()` guarded on the expected prior status `processing_status = 'received'`, and `!completed` is a failure. Receipt and outbox payloads pass through the shared `redactCredentialMaterial`; `payload_hash` still covers the unredacted signed payload. Route-local `resolveClaim`/`isBefore` only — no new shared primitive was invented and the shared helper was not edited.

defects_found: SIGNATURE: `MUSIC_LICENSING_WEBHOOK_ALLOW_UNSIGNED` unsigned processing pass, as above.

REPLAY: acknowledge-on-collision with no completion-marker read. The `invoice.paid` side effects (music_license_invoices.status='paid' plus the music_licensing_outbox insert) could be permanently skipped, so a paid licence invoice could stay unpaid.
COMPLETION: error-only check on the completion update; a zero-row update reported success.
REDACTION: full payload persisted verbatim in music_licensing_partner_events.payload.
per_route.fix: Same four fixes. Adaptations to this ledger's own vocabulary: the claim status is `verified` (now unconditional, since a signature is required), the failure marker is `rejected`, the completion guard is `.eq('status','verified')`, and the reclaim restores `status: 'verified'` with a bumped `received_at`. This deliberately stays inside the archived check constraint `status in ('received','verified','processed','rejected','duplicate')` rather than inventing a `processing` value, so the reclaim cannot violate the schema it will eventually run against.

defects_found: SIGNATURE: `MUSIC_RIGHTS_ADMIN_WEBHOOK_ALLOW_UNSIGNED` unsigned processing pass, as above.

REPLAY: acknowledge-on-collision with no completion-marker read. The `registration.status` side effects (music_rights_external_records insert plus the music_rights_admin_outbox insert keyed `reg-reconcile-<eventId>`) could be permanently skipped, so a provider status change would never be reconciled.
COMPLETION: error-only check on the completion update; a zero-row update reported success.

REDACTION: full payload persisted verbatim in BOTH music_rights_admin_partner_events.payload and music_rights_external_records.payload (the latter built by spreading the raw payload). This route had two durable verbatim copies, not one.
per_route.fix: Same four fixes, with the same `verified`/`rejected` vocabulary adaptation as licensing. `aggregate_id` was also repointed from the insert-time `stored.id` to the resolved `receiptRowId`, because on a resumed claim the insert returned no row and the outbox would otherwise have been written against a null aggregate.

required_to_enable: Database: additive forward-only migration restoring the three receipt ledgers (music_institutional_partner_events, music_licensing_partner_events, music_rights_admin_partner_events) plus every sibling the three routes write — music_institutional_outbox_events, music_licensing_outbox, music_rights_admin_outbox, music_rights_external_records, music_license_invoices, music_license_agreements. All six currently exist only as `local_only_unapplied` archive SQL. Apply additively, never `supabase db reset` (CP-051).

Database: the reclaim depends on `received_at timestamptz not null default now()` and `processed_at timestamptz` existing on all three ledgers, and on the status check constraints admitting the claim vocabulary above. This was verified against archived DDL only; no hosted table was queried and no such claim is made.

Release/Database: flip `advanced_music_webhooks` from 'disabled' to a launchable status in lib/config/launch-capabilities.ts. That single line is the entire launch gate, which is why the defects had to be removed now rather than at enablement time.
Release: provision per-provider `MUSIC_{INSTITUTIONAL,LICENSING,RIGHTS_ADMIN}_WEBHOOK_SECRET[_<PROVIDER>]` values. No unsigned path can be configured, so there is no fixture mode to preserve.

NOTE for the future enabler: `hashPayload` digests `JSON.stringify(payload)` of the *parsed* body, not the raw bytes, so `payload_hash` proves a canonical re-serialization rather than byte-exact body integrity. This is unchanged from INTG-009 and from the pre-existing `hashPayload` contract, and it is recorded rather than silently altered.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Classify and dispose every integrations-domain entry in the type inventory, recorded in the task record: canonical replacement, or dead-consumer deletion with a zero-use re-validation.
evidence: docs/engineering/database-type-inventory-2026-09-25.json codeDriftClusters entry owningDomain=integrations -> 1 object, 6 diagnostic hits, 1 object with a live consumer. The inventory file was read and NOT edited; the database lane owns it and TICKET-008 is live against it.

dispositions.disposition: NEITHER repoint NOR delete — the object must genuinely exist as schema. Raised to the database lane as HF-DB019-EVENT-PROVIDER-CONNECTIONS against the already-active DB-019 ('Close non-regenerable schema drift'), which is exactly this failure mode. Reported, not performed: no file was deleted, no route was repointed, and the inventory was not edited.
dispositions.zero_use_revalidation: FAILED as a dead-consumer candidate, on two independent grounds, and the inventory's own consumer list is wrong in a way that matters.
revalidation_detail: FALSE ATTRIBUTION: the inventory names app/api/hiring/apply/profile-preview/route.ts as a tscFile and a liveConsumer of event_provider_connections. Read in full, that file contains ZERO references to event_provider_connections — it queries only job_posting_templates and job_applications. Its tsc diagnostic belongs to `job_posting_templates.application_form_template`, a separate work-domain item in the same inventory. 1 of the 2 named live consumers is not a consumer.

UNDERSTATEMENT: a repository-wide search finds FIVE app-code consumers, not two — app/api/integrations/bandsintown/status/route.ts:16, app/api/integrations/bandsintown/connect/route.ts:40, app/api/integrations/bandsintown/disconnect/route.ts:25 and :37, app/api/events/[id]/claim/route.ts:61, and four references in app/api/cron/events/sync/route.ts (lines 154, 173, 186, 213). The other four do not appear in the inventory at all.

WHY THEY ARE MISSED, and why this matters more than the count: three of the five use `createServiceRoleClient()` and their `.from()` chain resolves through an untyped client, so they emit no tsc diagnostic and can never enter an inventory built from a preserved tsc log. The inventory is a floor derived from compiler output, not a liveness census.

LIVENESS OF THE FIVE, by the gate that actually protects each: bandsintown/status — REACHABLE, has no capability gate at all; it authenticates, queries, and returns `mode` (always 'disabled') with whatever rows come back. bandsintown/connect — permanently 503, `getBandsintownMode()` is 'disabled' because `external_event_providers` is 'disabled'. bandsintown/disconnect — REACHABLE and the sharpest of them: it is gated by session auth only, never by provider mode, and it reads then service-role-writes the table, so an authenticated caller can drive a real state change. events/[id]/claim — permanently 503, `isEventFeatureEnabled('EVENT_EXTERNAL_CLAIMS')` routes through the same disabled capability. cron/events/sync — permanently 503, explicit `isLaunchCapabilityAvailable('external_event_providers')` guard.

CONCLUSION: deletion is not an option (2 reachable consumers, 1 of them a service-role write path), and the repository records no canonical replacement (`canonicalReplacement: null`; no identity map names a destination). The only honest disposition is an additive forward-only migration. The archived DDL is complete and unambiguous, and every column any consumer selects is present in it, so no column-contract invention is required.
dispositions.exact_column_contract_supplied: id uuid pk default gen_random_uuid(); owner_type text not null check in ('artist','venue','organization'); owner_id uuid not null; provider text not null; external_identity text not null; display_name text; status text not null default 'pending' check in ('pending','active','error','disconnected'); connection_mode text not null default 'artist_owned_key' check in ('artist_owned_key','partner'); secret_reference text; scopes text[]; verified_at timestamptz; last_synced_at timestamptz; next_sync_at timestamptz; last_error_code text; created_by uuid not null references auth.users(id) on delete cascade; created_at timestamptz not null default now(); updated_at timestamptz not null default now(); unique (owner_type, owner_id, provider, external_identity); plus partial index on (provider, next_sync_at) where status = 'active'. Source: supabase/migration-archive/pre-reconciliation-local-only-2026-08-20/20260804130000_event_provider_foundation.sql lines 67-91. Note `secret_reference` is a pointer into the approved secret store and must stay a pointer — the archived DDL says so explicitly and INTG-007 makes that boundary fail-closed.

acceptance_criteria.collateral_finding_for_the_database_lane: The same blind spot explains why AC-1's three receipt ledgers are absent from the inventory: all three deferred partner routes (and both INTG-009 partner routes, and the Supabase notifications route) hold the service-role client as `let supabase: any` and therefore emit no type diagnostics at all. Verified: music_licensing_partner_events, music_rights_admin_partner_events, music_institutional_partner_events, music_rights_external_records, music_rights_admin_outbox, music_licensing_outbox, music_license_invoices, music_license_agreements, music_institutional_outbox_events, event_sync_jobs, event_claims and event_discovery_index are all absent from the inventory. The '1 object' integrations figure is therefore a lower bound on the domain's real type-drift exposure, not a measurement of it. Recorded for TICKET-008/DB-019; no inventory edit was made.

triaged_and_routed_not_registered.verdict: No defect. The reported guard is `if (code)` and the sink is `supabase.auth.exchangeCodeForSession(code)` at line 41 — the guard consumes the identical value the sensitive action consumes, so no separate authorization condition exists to bypass and the `else` branch at line 101 performs no code exchange. This is the same rule shape already dispositioned for #102 in Wave 33.
triaged_and_routed_not_registered.action: Routed, not registered. app/auth/** is not integrations-owned; registering an integrations-owned exception for another lane's file would be a governance claim this lane cannot make.

triaged_and_routed_not_registered.verdict: No defect. The guard is `if (type === 'recovery')` and the sensitive action is the redirect to /reset-password. The attacker-controlled `type` is itself the consumed value, and it has already been constrained to the ALLOWED_OTP_TYPES allowlist at line 28 and successfully verified by `verifyOtp` at line 38 before line 50 is reached, so the session is established by the time the branch runs. The value narrows paths rather than skipping a check.

No credential at rest. The value written to sessionStorage is `{ userId, profileId, accountType }` — identifiers, not secrets. sessionStorage is tab-scoped and dies with the tab, and the read-back at the call site is guarded by `parsed.userId !== userId`, so it is a UX pointer and not an authorization store.

No credential at rest. `sessionStorage.setItem('active_venue_id', venueId)` stores a venue identifier used only to preselect a venue in the UI; it confers no access, and venue scope is re-verified server-side at the data boundary.
